dash.about.text: Serafis is a free, open-source and strictly defensive tool. It never sends your files or data anywhere and only connects to the internet when you ask it to (catalog update, official download). It cannot promise that every file will be recovered.
dash.about.title: About Serafis
dash.catalog.status: Catalog version {version} ({date}) · {n} official tools for {families} ransomware families · {origin}
dash.catalog.title: Recovery tools catalog
dash.first_aid.isolate: If the attack may still be in progress, disconnect this computer from the network (unplug the cable, turn off Wi-Fi).
dash.first_aid.keep_notes: Keep the ransom notes (the files with the attackers' instructions): they help identify the ransomware.
dash.first_aid.no_delete: Do not delete, rename or "repair" the encrypted files: they may be recoverable in the future.
dash.first_aid.no_pay: Paying does not guarantee that you will get your files back.
dash.first_aid.no_restart_tools: Do not run tools downloaded from unknown sites that promise to decrypt your files.
dash.first_aid.title: First aid — do this now
dash.intro: Serafis guides you step by step after a ransomware attack: it analyses the damage without touching your files, tries to identify the ransomware, looks for verified official recovery tools and documents everything in a report. Take your time: nothing is done without your confirmation.
dash.progress.title: Your progress
dash.title: Welcome to SERAFIS
download.err.network: Download failed: check your connection or use the official page in your browser.
download.err.not_official: The download address is not an official domain for this tool.
download.err.redirect: The download was redirected to a non-official site and was stopped.
download.err.too_large: The file is larger than expected and the download was stopped.
ident.disclaimer: Identification is based on indicators that attackers can imitate or change. A 'strong' result means several independent indicators agree, not absolute certainty. Always confirm before using a decryptor.
ident.engines_unavailable: Engines not available: {engines} (optional YARA engine requires yara-python and rules in the Serafis data folder).
ident.external.help: To confirm, you can upload a ransom note or an encrypted sample to these free services (they are external websites: read their privacy policy, and never upload sensitive documents).
ident.intro: Serafis compares the indicators found (extensions, file-name patterns, ransom notes) with its recognition rules. The result is an estimate, not a certainty.
ident.manual.confirm: Use the selected family instead of the automatic identification? Choose it only if it was confirmed by a reliable source.
ident.manual.help: If a professional or an online service (for example ID Ransomware or No More Ransom Crypto Sheriff) identified the ransomware, you can select it here.
ident.manual.title: Do you already know the family?
ident.need_scan: Run the assessment first: identification uses its results.
ident.none: No known ransomware family could be identified from the available indicators.
ident.title: Identification
launch.allowed: Serafis can open the tool for you in a visible window.
launch.blocked.failure: Opening is blocked because a check failed.
launch.blocked.no_proof: Serafis will not open the tool itself because neither a trusted hash nor a valid vendor signature was confirmed. If you trust the official source, follow the official guide and run it manually.
level.possible.explain: Weak indicators only: treat this as a hypothesis.
level.probable.explain: Indicators point to this family but are not conclusive.
level.strong.explain: Several independent indicators point to this family.
link.title: Open web page
missing.ambiguous: Two or more families have similar scores: the identification is ambiguous.
missing.confirm_externally: Confirm the identification with an independent service or a professional before using any tool.
missing.no_files: No files were found in the selected folders.
missing.no_match: The indicators do not match any family in the rules.
missing.no_note: No ransom note was found: if you know where it is, add its folder to the analysis.
missing.no_suspicious: No file looks encrypted with known patterns.
missing.variant_unknown: The exact variant could not be determined: decryptors often support only some variants.
missing.weak_evidence: The evidence is not strong enough for a reliable identification.
nodecryptor.export_tip: Export the report to keep a record of the incident and share it with professionals or the police.
nodecryptor.intro: This is not the end: new decryptors are published over time, often when police seize the attackers' servers. Meanwhile:
nodecryptor.isolate: If there is still a risk of compromise, keep the device disconnected from the network.
nodecryptor.keep_encrypted: Keep all encrypted files: copy them to an external drive if possible.
nodecryptor.keep_notes: Keep the ransom notes: they will be needed to identify the ransomware and to use future tools.
nodecryptor.no_delete: Do not delete or reformat anything without a backup.
nodecryptor.no_promise: No one can guarantee that all files will be recovered.
nodecryptor.professional: For important data or business systems, contact a qualified incident-response professional and report the attack to the police.
nodecryptor.recheck: Check the catalog again periodically for new solutions.
nodecryptor.title: No verified compatible decryptor is currently available.
options.found: {n} official tool(s) found in the catalog.
options.intro: Official decryption tools from the catalog that match the identified family. Serafis lists only tools published by recognised sources such as No More Ransom and the security vendors themselves.
options.need_identification: Complete the assessment and identification first.
options.not_guaranteed: A listed tool does not guarantee recovery: it may support only some variants. Always test it on copies of a few files first.
options.sha_not_published: no reference value published by the source — the check will be marked as not available
options.title: Recovery options
rec.backups: After recovery, set up regular offline backups.
rec.change_passwords: From a clean device, change the passwords of accounts used on the affected computer.
rec.confirm_identification: Confirm the identification with an independent service before using any tool.
rec.isolate: Keep affected devices disconnected from the network until they are cleaned.
rec.keep_encrypted: Keep all encrypted files: future tools may recover them.
rec.no_pay_guarantee: Paying the ransom does not guarantee recovery and funds criminal activity.
rec.professional: Contact a qualified incident-response professional for important data.
rec.recheck_catalog: Check the Serafis catalog again periodically for new decryptors.
rec.report_police: Report the attack to the police (in Italy: Polizia Postale; in the EU: see No More Ransom).
rec.test_first: Always test a decryptor on copies before using it on all files.
recovery.check.bad_header: the file header does not match its type: probably still encrypted or damaged
recovery.check.unchanged: identical to the encrypted copy: not decrypted
recovery.check.unknown_type: file type not checkable automatically: open it to check
recovery.check.valid_header: the file header matches its type: decryption looks successful
recovery.err.copy: The file could not be copied.
recovery.err.copy_mismatch: The copy is not identical to the original and was discarded.
recovery.err.inside_workspace: Select original files, not files already inside the work folder.
recovery.err.launch: The tool could not be opened.
recovery.err.launch_unsupported: Opening tools is supported only on Windows. Run the tool manually.
recovery.err.not_file: One of the selected items is not a regular file.
recovery.err.too_large: One of the files is too large for a test (max 200 MB).
recovery.err.workspace: The work folder could not be created.
recovery.intro: A careful procedure: first a backup, then a test on copies of a few files, and only after a successful test the full recovery.
recovery.s1.a: Copy all encrypted files and ransom notes to an external drive or another safe location.
recovery.s1.b: Use a drive you can disconnect afterwards, so a still-active infection cannot reach it.
recovery.s1.c: Never work on the only copy of your data: decryptors can fail and damage files.
recovery.s1.confirm: I have made a backup of the encrypted files, or I understand the risk of continuing without one.
recovery.s1.d: Make sure the computer is free from active malware (scan it with an up-to-date antivirus) before decrypting.
recovery.s1.title: 1. Prepare a backup
recovery.s2.choose: Choose where to create the work folder
recovery.s2.help: Serafis creates a separate work folder where it copies the test files. The originals are never touched.
recovery.s2.title: 2. Create a work folder
recovery.s3.help: Select 2–5 encrypted files that are not important, preferably of different types (for example a .jpg and a .pdf). Serafis will copy them to the work folder and check that each copy is identical.
recovery.s3.title: 3. Choose some test files
recovery.s4.launch_confirm: Serafis will open the verified tool in its own visible window. You will control it directly. Use it ONLY on the work folder with the copies. Continue?
recovery.s4.manual: How to use {name} ({vendor}) on the test files:
recovery.s4.manual_confirm: Confirm that you have run the official tool on the copies in the work folder.
recovery.s4.no_solution: No tool selected. Without a verified decryptor, keep your files and check the catalog later.
recovery.s4.step.a: Read the official guide of the tool.
recovery.s4.step.b: Start the tool (Windows may ask for confirmation).
recovery.s4.step.c: Select ONLY the work folder "1_encrypted_copies" as the folder to decrypt; if the tool allows choosing an output folder, choose "2_decrypted_output".
recovery.s4.step.d: Disable any option that deletes the encrypted files after decryption.
recovery.s4.step.e: Write down any error message and come back here.
recovery.s4.title: 4. Run the test with the official tool
recovery.s5.help: For each test file, select the decrypted file produced by the tool. Serafis checks that it is no longer encrypted by looking at its header.
recovery.s5.problem_added: The problem has been recorded in the report.
recovery.s5.problems: Error messages or problems (they will be included in the report):
recovery.s5.title: 5. Check the results
recovery.s6.a: Make sure the backup of the encrypted files is complete and disconnected.
recovery.s6.b: Run the official tool on the remaining folders, a few at a time.
recovery.s6.c: Do not enable options that delete the encrypted originals.
recovery.s6.d: Check a sample of the decrypted files as you go.
recovery.s6.e: Keep the encrypted files until you are sure every important file was recovered.
recovery.s6.failed: At least one test failed. Do not run the tool on all your files: check the variant, read the official guide or contact the vendor or a professional.
recovery.s6.locked: The full recovery guide is available after at least one successful test and no failed test.
recovery.s6.title: 6. Full recovery
recovery.s6.unlocked: The test was successful. To recover all files:
recovery.title: Recovery

verify.hash.ok: The SHA-256 matches the trusted reference value.
verify.intro: Before using a decryptor, Serafis checks that it is authentic: official origin, SHA-256 hash, digital signature and compatibility.
verify.need_solution: Select a tool in the recovery options first.
verify.never_auto: Serafis never downloads or runs programs on its own. The download starts only if you authorise it, only from the official address, and the file is never executed automatically.
verify.sig.invalid: The digital signature is NOT valid (status: {status}).
verify.sig.not_pe: Signature check not applicable to this file type (for example an archive: extract it and verify the program).
verify.sig.not_signed: The file is NOT digitally signed.

verify.sig.unavailable: Signature check not available on this system ({reason}).
verify.sig.valid_unknown_signer: Valid signature by {subject}; no expected signer is recorded for this vendor.
verify.source.inconclusive: The recorded origin ({url}) is not a web address: origin cannot be confirmed.
verify.source.mismatch: The file comes from {url}, which is NOT an official domain ({domains}).
verify.source.unknown: The download address is unknown. Official domains: {domains}
